prompt:
Create a second high-fidelity desktop web-app UI concept at 1440×1000 for the same private social Teen Patti product and the same established clubhouse design system shown in the reference image. Preserve the identity exactly in spirit: near-black deep green page (#07110E), rich green felt (#163E2D), warm invitation gold (#E8B04A), warm ivory typography (#F6ECD8), dark lacquer brown rail (#2A1714), elegant high-contrast serif display headings paired with geometric sans-serif UI text, restrained soft shadows, tactile card-room materials, premium adult social atmosphere. This must clearly belong to the same product, but it must use a different information architecture from the reference.

Direction: PERSISTENT TABLE STAGE. Design the authenticated lobby first viewport around one dominant private friend table that occupies roughly 65% of the screen. Show a beautiful six-seat oval or rounded felt table with one occupied host seat and five empty friend seats arranged spatially around it. Integrate the persistent room code “ACE-482”, table name “Sunday Circle”, “1 of 6 seated”, privacy state “Friends only”, and a dominant gold “Share invite” action directly into the physical table rail so the table—not a dashboard card—is the main operating surface. Use a slim, quiet side rail for “Join with a code” and “Create a new table” only when relevant, plus a compact top navigation: Clubhouse, How to play, Profile. Show a restrained friend-arrival status such as “Invite copied · waiting for friends” without invented people or activity. Place “Practice & explore” behind a small secondary disclosure below the main stage; no public table grid. Make hierarchy, legibility, focus states, and action priority board-ready. No purchase UI, no fake testimonials, no popularity claims, no real-money language, no casino neon, no gradients, no glassmorphism. Use realistic crisp product copy. The result must look like a polished working web beta screenshot, not a moodboard, wireframe, poster, or marketing landing page.
